questions.question: A death benefit is settled at the end of the $1/m$-year interval containing death, with positive integer $m$. Increasing $m$ changes the settlement calendar. What happens to the total benefit amount for one death?
options: It remains one benefit; only its settlement date changes.
It is divided into m smaller payments after death.
It is paid once at every remaining boundary after death.
It becomes an amount proportional to the waiting time after death.

questions.question: A unit death benefit is paid at the end of the $1/m$-year interval of death, with positive integer $m$ and $\tau_m=\lceil mT\rceil/m$ for death time $T>0$. Why is the ceiling used rather than rounding to the nearest integer?
options: The selected boundary must be equally distant from both interval endpoints.
The selected boundary must minimise the absolute waiting distance.
The selected boundary must not occur before death.
The selected boundary must precede the next completed year.

questions.question: A death benefit uses $m=12$ in the settlement rule $\tau_m=\lceil mT\rceil/m$, where $T$ is years until death. What calendar spacing does this parameter specify?
options: Twelve years between possible settlement dates.
One twelfth of a year between possible settlement dates.
Twelve benefit payments for every death.
A waiting time of exactly one twelfth of a year after every death.

questions.question: A unit benefit uses positive integer frequency $m$. For integer $k\ge0$, let $S(t)=\mathbb{P}(T>t)$ for continuous death time $T$, and $v=(1+i)^{-1}$ for annual interest $i>-1$. Which factor should multiply $v^{(k+1)/m}$ in the APV sum?

For a continuous death time $T>0$ and interest $i>0$, put $v=(1+i)^{-1}$, $D=\mathbb{E}[v^T]$, $A_m=\mathbb{E}[v^{\lceil mT\rceil/m}]$ and $A_1=\mathbb{E}[v^{\lceil T\rceil}]$, with positive integer $m$. What ordering is guaranteed?
A unit death benefit uses quarterly settlement: $\tau_4=\lceil4T\rceil/4$. Death occurs at $T=2.13$ years. At what time is the benefit paid?

A continuous death time $T>0$ is settled at the next monthly boundary $\tau_{12}=\lceil12T\rceil/12$. Let waiting time be $W=\tau_{12}-T$. Which is the sharp one-interval range guaranteed almost surely for every continuous lifetime law?
A unit death benefit has semiannual settlement, death time $T=0.3$ years, and annual discount factor $v=0.81$. What is its realised present value?
Annual effective interest is $i=0.21$. Its nominal rate convertible twice yearly is defined by $i^{(2)}=2((1+i)^{1/2}-1)$. What is $i^{(2)}$?

UDD holds within every age-year. A unit whole-life benefit has annual-settlement APV $A=0.4$ at effective annual interest $i=0.21$. For semiannual settlement, $i^{(2)}=0.20$. What is its APV $A^{(2)}$?

Two ages have positive annual-settlement death-benefit APVs $A_x,A_y$. UDD holds in every subsequent year at both ages, and both use the same interest $i>0$ and frequency $m$, with nominal rate $i^{(m)}$. How do ratios $A_x^{(m)}/A_x$ and $A_y^{(m)}/A_y$ compare?
options: They agree only when the annual APVs agree.
The ratio is larger at the age with higher annual mortality.
They are equal even when the annual APVs differ.
Each ratio is inversely proportional to its own annual APV.

questions.question: For annual effective interest $i>0$, define nominal rate $i^{(m)}=m((1+i)^{1/m}-1)$ for positive integer $m$ and force $\delta=\log(1+i)$. What is the limit of $i^{(m)}$ as $m$ increases without bound?
A unit benefit is eventually paid for every finite death time, using any positive integer settlement frequency $m$. Assume death is finite almost surely and annual interest is zero. What is its APV?
options: Greater than one whenever settlement is more frequent than annual.
Less than one at every finite settlement frequency.
Equal to the expected waiting time after death.

questions.question: A continuous death time $T$ has survivor $S(0)=1,S(0.5)=0.8,S(1)=0$. A unit benefit uses semiannual settlement and annual discount factor $v=0.81$. What is its APV?

Under UDD in every year, a unit benefit has annual-settlement APV $A=0.4$ at annual effective interest $i=0.1$. Put $\delta=\log(1.1)$ and $v=1/1.1$. Which expression gives its APV $D$ for immediate payment at death?

Under UDD in every year, the fractional death-year part $R=T-\lfloor T\rfloor$ is uniform on $(0,1)$. A benefit uses quarterly settlement $\tau_4=\lceil4T\rceil/4$. What is the mean waiting time $W=\tau_4-T$?

Death time $T$ has a continuous density positive on $(0,1)$. A benefit is paid at $\tau_m=\lceil mT\rceil/m$. Does changing settlement frequency from $m=3$ to $m=4$ guarantee $\tau_4\le\tau_3$ almost surely?
options: Yes; shorter intervals put every new endpoint before an old endpoint.
No; the nonnested grids settle some deaths later at frequency four.
No; exact payment-boundary deaths have positive probability.
Yes; both first-year grids finish at the same date, time one.

questions.question: Under UDD, waiting $W$ to semiannual death settlement is uniform on $(0,0.5)$ and independent of completed death-year count $K$. At force $\delta=\log4$, define $L=\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{e}^{-\delta W}]$ and $R=\mathrm{e}^{-\delta\mathbb{E}[W]}$. Which comparison holds?
options: The sign of L-R depends on K.

questions.question: Model A has death time uniform on $(0,0.25)$ years; Model B has death time uniform on $(0.75,1)$ years. A unit benefit uses annual discount factor $v=0.81$. Both annual-settlement APVs are $0.81$. What are their semiannual-settlement APVs $(A_2,B_2)$?

A lifetime has survivor $S(t)=\mathrm{e}^{-t}$ for $t\ge0$. Annual discount factor is $v=\mathrm{e}^{1/2}>1$, so interest is negative. A unit benefit is paid at $\tau_2=\lceil2T\rceil/2$. Which approximate APV follows from the convergent death-bin sum?
